source_text.body:
Use OpenClaw for development, research and ad hoc tasks
A commenter runs OpenClaw agents for software development, research and ad hoc tasks, and has them show a Hermes instance how they did tasks so it can learn a more efficient way.
·
Aug 1, 2026
Done with
OC
OpenClaw
HA
Hermes Agent
What they did
The commenter says OpenClaw is their main tool for software development, research, and random ad hoc work. They added a Hermes instance on a lightweight LXC, and after OpenClaw agents complete a task, those agents show Hermes how they did it so Hermes can work on a more efficient method; the person also creates inputs such as a password list when needed.
How it went
They say this cut their OpenRouter spend and sped up one repeat workflow: getting a requested movie or TV show into Plex dropped from about 20–30 minutes to about 5 minutes. They note the network became the bottleneck at that point.
Worth knowing
The clearest catch is that the Hermes helper was a separate instance running on a lightweight LXC, and even after optimization the user’s network limited further gains.
Try it yourself
with
OpenClaw
Copy prompt
I want you to handle [recurring tasks, e.g. research briefs and small coding fixes] for me. After finishing each task, write down the steps you took in a short how-to note saved in [folder] so another agent could repeat it more efficiently. Done means the task result plus a clear note for each, and ask me before deleting files or sending messages.
Original source: https://www.reddit.com/r/openclaw/comments/1v2e5kr/what_do_you_use_openclaw_for_actual_use_case
